InnoBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the InnoBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this portion of the call, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss InnoBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Patel Singh, Chief Scientific Officer; and Maria Lopez, Head of Commercial.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of InnoBio Therapeutics.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. InnoBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our oncology portfolio and accelerating uptake of NovaSlim in the obesity and diabetes markets. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including advancing our late-stage clinical assets, optimizing our commercial execution, and strengthening our balance sheet.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on our overall results with key takeaways like double-digit revenue growth and margin expansion; the effectiveness of our marketing and sales efforts across regions; our geographic revenue breakdown with particular momentum in emerging markets; the evolving pricing and reimbursement dynamics; highlights from cash flow generation and balance sheet strength; and our updated revenue guidance alongside major upcoming catalysts such as PDUFA dates and Phase 3 readouts.

We are particularly excited about ONC-101 and its potential to deliver blockbuster growth through label expansions in additional oncology indications.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Ramirez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.65 billion, an increase of 22% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in our oncology and GLP-1 franchises, partially offset by pricing pressures.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $500 million, or $1.50 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $700 million, or $2.10 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.45 billion, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D to support our pipeline while maintaining operational efficiency. Our cash position remains strong at $2.8 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to net product sales of $10.8 billion to $11.2 billion.

Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'll now walk you through our Q3 2024 financial results, which underscore NovaBio Therapeutics' resilient execution amid a dynamic biotech landscape—wait, InnoBio's resilient execution. Overall, we delivered a standout quarter, exceeding consensus expectations across key metrics and positioning us for sustained momentum into 2025. Let me highlight the numbers and drivers before sharing our strategic takeaways.

Total net product revenues reached $2.82 billion—aligning with our blended figures—up 22% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, handily beating our guidance midpoint. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth, fueled by blockbuster contributions from our core oncology and rare disease franchises. Excluding COVID-19 monoclonal antibody tailwinds—which have now fully normalized at under 2% of revenues—our underlying growth was a robust 19%.

Gross margins expanded to 84.2%, a 210-basis-point improvement from Q3 2023, driven by manufacturing efficiencies at our Singapore biologics facility and a favorable mix shift toward high-margin antibody-drug conjugates, or ADCs. Operating expenses rose 12% to $1.45 billion, reflecting targeted R&D investments, but we maintained OpEx discipline, delivering non-GAAP operating income of $1.12 billion—up 28% YoY. Non-GAAP diluted EPS came in at $1.78, surpassing the Street's estimate. Cash flow from operations was a healthy $1.4 billion, bolstering our balance sheet to $8.2 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable securities—scaling to our pro forma $2.8 billion core position. We also repurchased $500 million in shares under our ongoing authorization, signaling confidence in our intrinsic value.

Our oncology portfolio, which accounts for 62% of revenues, was the growth engine, surging 31% YoY to $1.75 billion. Flagship ONC-101, our next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific akin to leading profiles, posted strong sales on the back of expanded labels in NSCLC and melanoma. Complementing this, our other inhibitors generated solid growth, benefiting from real-world evidence. Rare diseases contributed meaningfully, led by our AAV-based gene therapies. Legacy assets grew modestly amid biosimilar pressures.

R&D remains our North Star, with investments yielding tangible milestones like positive topline data from key trials and new partnerships. U.S. revenues soared 28% to represent the majority, propelled by payer access wins; Europe grew steadily despite pricing pressures; Asia-Pacific accelerated via key partnerships; emerging markets contributed with biosimilar ramps.

In a market digesting GLP-1 dominance, we're capitalizing on oncology's resilience. We've navigated biosimilar headwinds proactively. Key takeaways: double-digit revenue growth, margin expansion, and a de-risked pipeline set us up for 20-22% top-line growth in FY2025, with narrowed EPS guidance. We're raising our full-year revenue outlook accordingly. Challenges like tariff risks are on our radar, but our manufacturing footprint insulates us.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now dive into our Q3 geographic revenue performance, which underscores the resilience of our core markets and the accelerating momentum in emerging regions. For the quarter, total net product sales reached $2.48 billion—core to our $2.65 billion total—up 14% year-over-year on a reported basis and 16% at constant exchange rates. Let me break this down by geography, highlighting key drivers, headwinds, and our strategic positioning.

Starting with our largest market, the United States represented 56% of total revenue, or $1.39 billion, growing 15% year-over-year. This strength was propelled by robust demand for our flagship GLP-1 receptor agonist, NovaSlim, which continues to capture share in the burgeoning U.S. obesity and diabetes market—much like we've seen with leaders such as Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy. Volume growth of 18% more than offset a modest 3% price erosion from PBM rebates and 340B discounting. Oncology contributions from our PD-1 inhibitor, ONC-101, added another layer, with U.S. sales up 22% amid expanded label indications for NSCLC and melanoma.

Europe accounted for 24% of revenues, or $595 million, which was essentially flat year-over-year at constant rates. Here, we faced familiar headwinds: pricing pressures from HTA bodies like NICE in the UK and IQWiG in Germany, coupled with delays in joint clinical assessments under the new EU HTA Regulation. That said, our biosimilar portfolio ramped up post-patent expiry, delivering 12% volume growth. We expect sequential improvement in Q4 as tenders in Spain and Italy finalize.

The Rest of World, or ROW, segment contributed 20% of total revenues, at $495 million, up a stellar 28% year-over-year. Within ROW, our emerging markets—defined as China, India, Brazil, Southeast Asia, and Middle East & Africa—were the standout performer, surging 35% to $385 million, or 15.5% of total sales. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth in EMs, outpacing the broader pharma market's estimated 8-10% expansion in these regions per IQVIA data.

China led the charge at 42% of EM revenues, up 45% YoY, with tender success for our insulin biosimilar and NMPA approval for ONC-101. India contributed strongly, driven by CDMO partnerships and generic launches. Latin America saw solid growth with reimbursement wins. Southeast Asia and MENA rounded out with tender wins and approvals.

Our EM growth results from a multi-year playbook: investments in localized manufacturing like our Suzhou JV, real-world data platforms, and partnerships. Looking forward, we guide EM growth of 30-35% for FY24, with China scaling significantly. Risks include forex and tenders, but our R&D allocation positions us well.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a transformative year, I'd like to dive into our full-year revenue guidance and highlight the key upcoming catalysts that will drive our trajectory into 2025 and beyond. Our team has executed exceptionally well against our strategic priorities in oncology, cardiovascular gene therapies, and our emerging neurology pipeline, positioning us for sustained double-digit growth amid a dynamic industry landscape.

We're raising our full-year 2024 net product sales guidance to $2.65 billion to $2.75 billion for the quarter context, representing approximately 28% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, up from prior ranges—scaling to full-year $10.8-11.2 billion. This uplift reflects stronger-than-expected U.S. demand for ONC-101, which generated substantial year-to-date sales driven by deeper penetration and new indications. Ex-U.S. sales have accelerated, fueled by reimbursement wins.

For Q4 specifically, we guide to strong sequential growth. Breaking it down: ONC-101 leadership, CAR-T contributions, royalties and milestones. Regionally, ex-U.S. mix improves. For 2025, initial expectations at 27-30% growth, assuming stable margins.

Key upcoming catalysts: Q4 2024 PDUFA for ONC-101 label expansion in MSI-high endometrial cancer, with strong Phase 3 data; H1 2025 topline from CARDIOVAX-3 in HCM gene therapy; mid-2025 partnership milestones and manufacturing scale-up; longer-term events like NeuroShield-1 in Alzheimer's and siRNA in NASH.

Strategically, we're leaning into combo therapies and precision medicine, with ample cash supporting R&D. In summary, our raised guidance reflects excellence, and these catalysts provide clear line-of-sight to blockbuster status.

Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. I'll now walk you through our third-quarter cash flow and balance sheet highlights, which underscore the strength of our commercial engine and our disciplined capital allocation.

We ended the quarter with cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaling $2.8 billion, up sequentially and providing 28 months of runway. Net cash at $2.4 billion after debt, with optimized profile via tender offer reducing maturities. Net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.6x, among the lowest in peers.

Current assets at $4.2 billion, working capital strong. Operating cash flow exceptional at $925 million, up 32% YoY, propelled by ONC-101 and NovaSlim. Investing outflows for R&D capex and partnerships. Free cash flow record at $725 million, enabling repurchases, paydowns, and dividends.

Regionally, U.S. dominant, Europe steady, EMs growing fast. This positions us for M&A, mitigating patent cliffs via milestones. Cash conversion improved. We're raising FY24 FCF guidance to $2.6-2.8 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to provide a detailed update on the pricing and reimbursement landscape, which remains a critical driver of our top-line performance and margin profile. Navigating this requires agility and value demonstration. I'll break it down by region for our portfolio, particularly oncology with ONC-101 and NovaSlim.

U.S., 65% of revenue, net price at 72% of WAC, down modestly due to PBM rebates and IRA. ONC-101 robust but ASP declining; positives in NovaSlim coverage. Europe stable with tender discounts; key HTA wins in Germany, France, UK, Japan. EMs volume offsets lower pricing; NRDL in China.

Biosimilar erosion trend pressuring originators. Initiatives: VBA platform, RWE investments, AI pricing, patient assistance. Guide flat U.S. net price growth, positive ex-U.S. Long-term, premium pricing via data.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Rachel Kim, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, ONC-101's EMBARK-2 Phase 3 showed compelling ORR and PFS in endometrial cancer, on track for PDUFA. Our CARDIOVAX-3 gene therapy for HCM demonstrated significant LVOT reduction in Phase 2. CAR-T manufacturing improvements support expanded access. We expect to report topline data from NeuroShield-1 interim in Q3 2025 and BLA submissions for multiple assets by year-end. These milestones de-risk our pipeline and unlock substantial value.

Next, Dr. Patel Singh will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Patel Singh, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo editing for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is enrolling rapidly, aided by AI-optimized stratification that has cut timelines by 25%. The siRNA platform for NASH fibrosis shows promise in preclinical models. We've advanced mRNA extensions for oncology and forged co-development pacts for bispecific T-cell engagers. Continuous bioprocessing boosts yields for ADCs, de-risking scale-up. Our HelixAI platform drives discoveries across modalities.

Now I'll turn the call over to Maria Lopez, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Maria Lopez, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with 22% overall growth. We are seeing strong uptake in ONC-101 across NSCLC and melanoma segments and NovaSlim ramping to 12-15% share in GLP-1s.

Thank you, CEO—Alex. Moving now to our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics, which continue to demonstrate robust execution across our portfolio, including our flagship immuno-oncology asset, ONC-101, our GLP-1 agonist NovaSlim for type 2 diabetes and obesity, and our gene therapy platform for rare neuromuscular disorders. I'll walk you through the key KPIs, trends, regional nuances, and the strategic levers we're pulling to drive sustainable growth.

First, on sales force productivity. Our field team of 1,200 representatives—optimized through our 2023 realignment—delivered a 12% year-over-year increase in average daily HCP details, reaching 9.2 calls per rep per day, up from 8.2 last year. This was fueled by our AI-powered territory management tool, integrated with Veeva CRM, which uses predictive analytics to prioritize high-decile oncologists and endocrinologists based on historical prescribing patterns and IQVIA TRx data. Conversion metrics are equally strong: new Rx share for ONC-101 in NSCLC climbed to 28% from 24% YoY, while total Rx held steady at 32%, despite biosimilar erosion. For NovaSlim, amid the GLP-1 surge, our NRx grew 45% YoY to 15% segment share, with reps closing 22% of targeted formulary discussions—ahead of peers.

Marketing ROI remains a standout, with blended ROAS hitting 4.8x, up from 4.2x. Patient services like NovaSlim Adherence Hub boosted persistence to 72%, adding $45 million in revenue. CAC dropped 15% to $2,800 per new prescriber via PrescribeAI.

Digital effectiveness: website traffic up 38% to 4.2 million visitors, 14% conversion; SOV 29% in oncology; email open rates 42%. VR CME for NovaSlim at 95% completion.

Regionally: U.S. (82% of sales) NRx +18%, payer wins key; EU challenged but NICE approvals lift TRx 14%; EMs +28% TRx via partnerships and Access Accelerator.

Strategic insights: 15% of $1.2 billion budget in next-gen like RWE campaigns highlighting OS advantage, omnichannel 360 Engage, DTC pilots. KOLs up 22% to 450.

Forward, 10-12% productivity gains, digital ROAS to 5.5x. Risks payer pushback, but data-centric approach outpaces peers.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Maria. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Chen with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

David Chen, Morningstar:
Thanks for taking my question. On the raised guidance, can you elaborate on the key assumptions around ONC-101 uptake and any conservatism baked in for IRA impacts?

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Great question, David. Our guidance uplift primarily reflects ONC-101's stronger-than-expected U.S. demand and ex-U.S. acceleration from reimbursement wins in Germany and Japan. We've embedded modest 4-5% gross-to-net erosion from payer shifts and 340B, but ONC-101's orphan status shields it from near-term IRA caps. We're comfortable with the midpoint implying 28% growth, with conservatism on EM tender volatility—70% hedged on forex.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel, Goldman Sachs:
Hi, team. Regarding emerging markets growth, how sustainable is the 35% surge, especially in China with NRDL risks?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thanks, Lisa. EM momentum is durable, driven by localized manufacturing like our Suzhou JV and partnerships yielding 45% China growth from tenders and ONC-101 launches. NRDL inclusion de-risks via KOLs and RWE; we guide 30-35% FY24 growth, outpacing IQVIA's 8-10% market. Supply chain diversification and 15% EM R&D keep us ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera, JPMorgan:
On clinicals, thoughts on the endometrial PDUFA for ONC-101 and competition in MSI-high?

Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer:
Mike, EMBARK-2 topline was robust: 48% ORR, 14-month PFS vs. 9 months, clean safety mirroring peers. This taps a $2 billion underserved market; approval could add $400-500 million peak U.S. sales by 2027, differentiating via bispecific mechanism over standard IO.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee, Barclays:
Marketing-wise, how is digital ROAS scaling, and any updates on NovaSlim DTC pilots?

Maria Lopez, Head of Commercial:
Sarah, digital ROAS at 6.2x drove blended 4.8x; targeting 5.5x in 2025 with generative AI personalization. NovaSlim DTC pilots mirror Novo strategies, projecting 3x ROAS, boosting persistence via Adherence Hub—already 72% vs. class average. Omnichannel lifts scripts 19%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Harris with RBC Capital. Please go ahead.

Tom Harris, RBC Capital:
Balance sheet looks fortress-like—any M&A pipeline or pipeline prioritization shifts?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Tom, $2.8 billion cash gives $1.2 billion dry powder for bolt-ons in cell/gene, like recent Aura acquisition synergies. No dilution needed; FCF $2.6-2.8 billion FY24 funds R&D $800 million, prioritizing ONC-101 follow-ons and gene therapies over non-core divestitures.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the InnoBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
